Concise Clinical Note

Consult Summary:
• 53-year-old man with 1-week painless swelling over the left olecranon; exam shows mild warmth and preserved motion – most consistent with aseptic olecranon bursitis.  

History:
• Presenting complaint: New swelling over left elbow noticed in the shower ~1 week ago; feels slightly warm, minimally tender adjacent to tip; no significant pain, erythema, or functional loss.  
• Denies trauma, overuse awareness, fever, or prior episodes.  
• Review of systems: No systemic symptoms (fever, malaise); full upper-limb function maintained.  
• Pertinent negatives: No known eczema, no other dry-skin areas, no redness spreading, no family rheumatologic history reported.  
• Past medical history: GP-diagnosed osteoarthritis (details not specified).  
• Allergies: Peanut allergy; no known drug allergies.  
• Medications: None.  
• Social / lifestyle: Desk job; runs 2–3 ×/week; otherwise healthy and active.  

Examination:
• Video inspection: Visible fluctuant swelling over olecranon; overlying skin slightly dry; surrounding area mildly warm; minimal tenderness lateral to tip; full range of elbow motion.  
• No marked erythema, no obvious cellulitis, no systemic distress.  
• Vitals: Not recorded.  

Impression:
• Primary: Aseptic (non-infectious) olecranon bursitis – classic presentation with localized swelling, slight warmth, preserved function, and absence of systemic signs.  
• Differential considerations:  
  – Septic olecranon bursitis: less likely but must be excluded; warmth present but no redness, severe pain, or systemic features.  
  – Gouty olecranon bursitis: possible given age/sex; no prior gout history but serum urate ordered.  

Plan:
• Pharmacologic: Ibuprofen 400 mg PO BID with food as anti-inflammatory; stop if gastrointestinal side-effects occur.  
• Investigations: Mail-out blood-test kit for CBC, ESR/CRP, rheumatologic panel, serum urate, and infectious markers.  
• Follow-up: Arrange review (video or face-to-face) ~6 days after tests to reassess elbow and review results.  
• Safety-net: Seek urgent care if elbow becomes very red, increasingly painful, swelling spreads, or systemic symptoms (fever) develop – concern for septic arthritis.  

Quality checks
● Missing expected elements: vitals, full medication list confirmation (OTC, supplements), immunization status (tetanus), detailed OA history.  
● Transcript/DDx conflicts: None noted.  
● Transcript quality: Clear but lacked vitals and some background details; minor audio fillers removed for clarity.
